findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and get cancelled
findings.body: All four goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) build their timeout context from the incoming request ctx (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which typically happens before the goroutine completes. The legacy write will then fail with context canceled, silently dropping the legacy copy that mode 3 exists to maintain. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (preserving auth/user values) as the parent before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Storage error path records legacy duration metric
findings.body: In Create, when `d.Storage.Create` fails the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` even though the failing call was to unified storage. Same in Update (line 129). This mislabels failures: storage error rates/latencies will be missing and legacy metrics will be polluted with storage failures. Should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Delete success passes object name as the 'kind' metric label
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource name instead of `options.Kind`. Since the name is unbounded per-object, this creates an unbounded-cardinality Prometheus label, risking memory blowup in the metrics registry, and makes the metric unusable for per-kind aggregation.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records storage duration
findings.body: The goroutine measuring the legacy DeleteCollection calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`, so legacy delete-collection latency/errors are never recorded and storage metrics are double-counted with legacy timings.

findings.title: Delete puts the un-enriched logger in the context
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses the base logger rather than `log`, so downstream code logging from the context loses the name/kind/method values that every other method in this file propagates.

findings.title: Legacy Update receives the raw objInfo, re-applying the patch against the legacy object
findings.body: The previous implementation wrapped objInfo with the already-updated object (`updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}`) before calling legacy. Now the raw `objInfo` is passed, so legacy will call `UpdatedObject` against its own stored object. For patch/apply requests this can produce a different result than what was written to unified storage (and resourceVersion precondition checks are evaluated against legacy's RV), causing the two stores to diverge or the legacy update to fail with a conflict.

findings.title: Tests never synchronize with the async legacy write
findings.body: Mode 3 now performs the legacy write in a goroutine, but the tests return immediately after the storage call. Nothing asserts that Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is invoked, so the core behaviour of this PR is untested. Worse, the shared `mock.Mock` is read/written by the goroutine after the test function finishes, which is a data race (will fail under -race) and can cause 'mock called after test completion' panics. Add a synchronization hook (e.g. a channel/WaitGroup signalled from the mock's Run function) and assert the legacy calls.

findings.title: Local registry shadows package-level one inconsistently
findings.body: `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` inside TestMode3_Get shadows the package-level `p` used by every other test here, while the mode1 test removed exactly this pattern. All other subtests reuse one global registry across many NewDualWriter calls; if the metrics registration uses MustRegister this repeated registration of the same collectors will panic. Pick one approach (fresh registry per test is safest) and apply it consistently.

findings.title: Unrelated and duplicated go.work.sum entries
findings.body: This PR adds ~16 go.work.sum lines unrelated to the dual-writer change, including a duplicate `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod` entry that already exists two lines above. These look like accidental local-tooling churn and should be dropped from the PR.
